module_title: Intermediate Timeline - Ramayana Circuit, Braj Traditions, and Cultural Mahotsavs
introduction: This level covers fairs deeply rooted in the Ramayana and Mahabharata epics, localized Braj traditions, and state-sponsored cultural festivals (Mahotsavs). These form the core of 'Match the Following' questions in RO/ARO and UPPSC Prelims.

core_concepts.title: Fairs of the Braj (Mathura) Region
core_concepts.description:
- **Lathmar Holi:** Barsana (Mathura) - Celebrated in the Hindu month of Phalguna.
- **Mudiya Purnima Mela:** Govardhan (Mathura) - Also known as Mudiya Poono; a massive circumambulation (Parikrama) fair.
- **Haridas Jayanti Mela:** Vrindavan (Mathura) - Dedicated to Swami Haridas, the legendary classical musician and guru of Tansen.

core_concepts.title: Ramayana Circuit Fairs
core_concepts.description:
- **Ramayan Mela:** Held in both Ayodhya and Chitrakoot.
- **Shringverpur Mela:** Farrukhabad (Historically significant as the site where Lord Rama crossed the Ganga with Nishadraj).
- **Parikrama Mela:** Naimisharanya (Sitapur) - Closely associated with Lord Rama's exile and ancient sages.

core_concepts.title: Other Historic and Agrarian Fairs
core_concepts.description:
- **Dadri Mela:** Ballia - Another massive **Cattle/Animal Fair** (second in importance only to Bateshwar).
- **Kampil Mela:** Farrukhabad - Deeply significant for Jains (associated with Lord Vimalnath) and Hindus alike.
- **Shakumbhari Devi Mela:** Saharanpur - Held twice a year during the Navratris.

core_concepts.title: Prominent Cultural Mahotsavs
core_concepts.description:
- **Ayurveda Mahotsav:** Jhansi.
- **Sulh-e-Kul Mahotsav:** Agra (Started historically by Emperor Akbar as a festival of universal peace and Hindu-Muslim unity).
- **Taj Mahotsav:** Agra (Held annually in February, showcasing Mughal heritage, arts, and crafts).
- **Kajri Mahotsav:** Mirzapur (Celebrating the folk monsoon singing tradition of Kajri).

important_entities.name: Naimisharanya (Sitapur)
important_entities.significance: Located in Sitapur, Naimisharanya hosts the famous Parikrama Mela. According to Puranic lore, 88,000 sages performed penance here, and it is the site where Maharishi Ved Vyas compiled the Puranas.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Kajri vs. Kajali Phonetic Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
This is a classic UPPSC trap designed to catch students who read too fast:
- **Kajri Mahotsav** ➡️ Mirzapur (Celebrates the monsoon folk song).
- **Kajali Mahotsav** ➡️ Mahoba (A distinct festival celebrated in the Bundelkhand region).
Watch the spelling carefully!

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: This phonetic link helps you instantly recall the two major historically distinct fairs hosted by the Farrukhabad district.

exam_strategy_tips: In RO/ARO matching grids, examiners frequently pair 'Dadri Mela' with Ballia and 'Shakumbhari Devi' with Saharanpur. Note carefully: Bateshwar (Agra) and Dadri (Ballia) are both animal fairs, do not confuse them with regular religious gatherings.
